title: Ekström wins a wet Red Bull Ring Race 2 as Scheider is disqualified
dek: Mattias Ekström won Race 2 from pole by 4.334 seconds from Gary Paffett and took the championship lead, while Timo Scheider was disqualified for the last-lap contact that sent Wickens and Wehrlein into the gravel.

chapters.title: From sunshine to a soaked Sunday
text: Saturday's opener had gone to Edoardo Mortara, who turned pole into victory by 1.792 seconds after Jamie Green's Audi lost its gearshift while leading. Pascal Wehrlein's second place made him the youngest leader of the DTM standings, on 94 points ahead of Mattias Ekström (86), Mortara (83) and Green (81).

Sunday promised something very different. After a dry, sunny Saturday, heavy rain arrived over the Styrian hills, and the second race was a full hour long, with a mandatory pit stop. Green, who was without points for the fourth race running, had a lot to recover and a grid set on a flooded track to do it from.

chapters.title: Ekström pips Rockenfeller by 0.005 seconds
text: The rain had eased by the time qualifying started, but the track was still extremely wet, with streams of water running across it, and the drivers began cautiously. Ekström found the time at the last moment: he lapped in 1:42.010 to take pole by just 0.005 seconds from Mike Rockenfeller's Audi, and said he had benefited from following in Gary Paffett's tracks on his final two attempts.

Paffett was third for Mercedes-AMG, 0.145 seconds back, and complained that he had hardly had a clear lap. Wehrlein started fourth and Robert Wickens fifth, so Mercedes drivers held third, fourth and fifth on the grid. Saturday's winner Mortara could not repeat his form and was sixth, ahead of Timo Scheider, with Christian Vietoris, Paul di Resta (who struggled in the conditions) and Adrien Tambay completing the top ten.

Green could manage only 17th. BMW had another poor session: Martin Tomczyk was the best of them in 14th, António Félix da Costa started 18th, and the last five places on the grid, from Bruno Spengler in 20th to Timo Glock in 24th, were all taken by BMWs.

chapters.title: A delayed start behind the safety car
text: Because of the heavy rain the start was delayed and the field left the grid behind the safety car, which stayed out for the opening laps. Once the race went green Ekström got away well and began to pull clear of Rockenfeller and Paffett. Paffett soon got past the Phoenix Audi for second place, with a bold move around the outside, and began to chase.
Elsewhere the conditions caught several drivers out. Vietoris and di Resta both took early trips through the gravel, and Wehrlein had a couple of off-track moments that cost him ground.

chapters.title: Paffett closes, Mortara moves up
text: The mandatory stops came on successive laps, with Paffett in first and Ekström a lap after him, by which point Paffett had already trimmed the gap. Mortara, who had started sixth, took advantage in the stop window to pass Rockenfeller and move onto the podium places. Nico Müller, who had started 11th, was on his way to fifth.

After the stops Ekström rebuilt his margin, but Paffett began a second charge in the final third of the race, and in the closing minutes the Mercedes was close enough to put the Audi driver under real pressure.

chapters.title: Ekström holds on, and a last-lap collision
text: Ekström found more in reserve, set the fastest lap of the race on lap 31 and edged the gap back out to take the flag after 34 laps 4.334 seconds ahead of Paffett. Mortara was third, 23.555 seconds behind, with Rockenfeller fourth and Müller fifth. Lucas Auer, who had started 16th, was sixth in front of his home crowd, followed by Maximilian Götz, Vietoris, di Resta and Félix da Costa, who took the final point in tenth.

The drama came on the last lap. Wickens had been holding up Scheider for several laps while Wehrlein closed in, and at the start of the final lap Müller was clear of Wickens, Scheider and Wehrlein. Wehrlein passed both at Turn 2, but at Turn 3 Scheider ran into the back of Wickens' Mercedes, which in turn hit Wehrlein, and both went into the gravel trap. They were classified 20th and 21st, a lap down. Scheider crossed the line sixth but was later disqualified. On the Audi radio, Wolfgang Ullrich could be heard calling "Timo, push him out" moments before the collision.

chapters.title: A championship lead, and a scandal
text: Ekström's second win of the season put him top of the championship on 111 points, 13 ahead of Mortara on 98. Wehrlein, who had led the standings for only a day, dropped to third on 94, ahead of Green (81), who was classified 17th and had now gone five races without scoring. Paffett's second place moved him up to 61 points, ahead of Wickens on 57. Ekström said that he had to give everything as Paffett came closer, and that experience counts for a lot in the wet. BMW's only point came from Félix da Costa, and only because of the disqualification.

The radio call dominated the paddock. Ullrich, the head of Audi Motorsport, apologised to Mercedes: he said he did not normally speak to drivers by radio, did not know the channel was open, and that the shout was a reaction in the heat of the moment rather than an instruction. Mercedes motorsport chief Toto Wolff said that anyone who had sent such a message should never go near a racetrack again, and that removing the championship leader was unacceptable. Scheider said he had not heard any message and that Wickens had braked hard in front of him.

The stewards disqualified Scheider because the telemetry and video indicated that the collision had been caused deliberately; the Phoenix team did not appeal. The radio call was referred to the sports court of the German motorsport federation DMSB, which ruled on 26 August. It banned Ullrich from the pit lane and team radio for the rest of the 2015 season, suspended Scheider from the Moscow round, fined Audi 200,000 euros and deleted the 62 manufacturers' points Audi had scored in Race 2, which dropped it behind Mercedes in the manufacturers' standings. Audi said it respected the verdict, did not appeal, and considered the case closed.
With ten of the 18 races run, the championship moved on to Moscow Raceway on 29–30 August, with Ekström in front, Mortara 13 points behind and Wehrlein 17, and Scheider serving his suspension.

facts.v: Heavy rain delayed the start of Race 2, which began behind the safety car before Ekström pulled away from pole.
